# Events: hear what happens, online and offline

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The events port, the router with its handlers and actions, and the in-memory port.

## `events`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/events.rs`)

Events for apps, online and offline (docs/sdk/events.md; F-SDK-188).

An app registers interest in named events through an [`EventsPort`] and handles them with an [`EventRouter`]. The core decides who
hears what: an app gets an event only if it registered for it and holds its scope, in order, with a sequence number that only grows
and a time. What happened while the app was not running waits in a bounded queue and arrives at the next start, before the first
frame, marked `late`; events that were dropped (the queue was full, too old, or too noisy) come as one `missed` marker. A payload
never carries a secret.

A handler *acts* through [`EventActions`]: it can keep state in the app itself, leave a note in the inbox, start a flow or call a
chat tool; the host binds those to the core, so a tool that changes something asks the person as it always does.

[`MemEvents`] is the in-memory port for tests and the browser preview. It follows the core's rules (scope, registration, order,
late, missed, coalescing, age, rate), with a clock the test moves.

### struct `PermissionChange`

What changed in what an app may do (the event `app.permissions`): names only.

```rust
pub struct PermissionChange
```

Public fields:

- `pub granted: Vec<String>`: Capabilities and scopes the app was given since it last heard.
- `pub revoked: Vec<String>`: Capabilities and scopes taken away.
- `pub dropped: Vec<String>`: Events the app had registered for that ended with a scope it lost.
- `pub effective: Vec<String>`: What the app holds now, and how many names that is (the list may be cut).
- `pub held: usize`
- `pub by: String`: `person`, `administrator`, `policy`, `store` or `expiry`.
- `pub restart: bool`: The app must restart (or register again) to use what changed.

### trait `EventsPort`

What an app is handed to hear events. The core's side is `iyakki_core_api::AppEvents`; the shell adapter binds this to it.

```rust
pub trait EventsPort
```

Methods:

- `fn register(&mut self, event: &str, filter: &str) -> Result<(), EventsError>`: Register (again is fine). Refused with a sentence when the app lacks the scope or the event is off.
- `fn unregister(&mut self, event: &str, filter: &str) -> Result<(), EventsError>`
- `fn registrations(&mut self) -> Vec<EventReg>`
- `fn start(&mut self) -> Vec<AppEvent>`: The app starts: the `missed` marker (if any), then everything that waited, `late` as recorded.
- `fn stop(&mut self)`: The app goes to the back or closes: from now on events wait.
- `fn poll(&mut self, max: usize) -> Vec<AppEvent>`: What arrived since the last call.
- `fn replay(&mut self, after_seq: u64) -> Vec<AppEvent>`: The delivered events after this number, again (after a crash before they were handled).
- `fn publish(&mut self, name: &str, payload: EvPayload) -> Result<usize, EventsError>`: Publish `custom.<this app>.<name>` for other apps.
- `fn capabilities(&mut self) -> Vec<String>  // has a default`: The names of what this app may do now (capabilities and scopes): read it again after an `app.permissions` event instead of keeping a copy.

### trait `EventActions`

What a handler may do. The host binds each to the core; a tool call goes through the normal approval path.

```rust
pub trait EventActions
```

Methods:

- `fn notify(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<(), String>`: Leave a note in the inbox (needs the `notify` capability; the person sees it). The refusal is a sentence.
- `fn start_flow(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<(), String>`: Start a flow by name (the core's flows; a flow that changes something asks as always).
- `fn call_tool(&mut self, tool: &str, args: &str) -> Result<String, String>`: Ask for a chat tool to run, with its arguments (JSON text). Nothing runs at once: the core puts the request in the person's waiting list and answers with a line saying so; the tool runs only if the person approves the card that names this app and the tool.

### struct `EventRouter`

Registers an app's interests and hands each event to its handler, in order, never twice.

An app that registers handles `missed` ([`EventRouter::on_missed`]) and looks at `late` (a late event is news that may be old: do not
ring a bell for a call that ended an hour ago); `app-check` says so when it does not.

```rust
pub struct EventRouter
```

Public fields:

- `pub unhandled: Vec<String>`: Events no handler took (a registration without a handler is a bug of the app).

Methods:

- `pub fn new() -> EventRouter`
- `pub fn on(mut self, event: &str, handler: impl FnMut(&AppEvent, &mut dyn EventActions) + 'static) -> EventRouter`: Interest in one event; the handler runs for every event of that name.
- `pub fn on_prefix(mut self, event: &str, prefix: &str, handler: impl FnMut(&AppEvent, &mut dyn EventActions) + 'static) -> EventRouter`: Like [`EventRouter::on`] for an event that takes a prefix (a settings key, a folder).
- `pub fn on_permissions(mut self, mut handler: impl FnMut(&PermissionChange, &AppEvent, &mut dyn EventActions) + 'static) -> EventRouter`: What the app does when what it may do changed (a permission granted, taken away, or a registration dropped with its scope). The event always comes: no registration, no scope, and the person cannot switch it off. Read `port.capabilities()` again here.
- `pub fn on_missed(mut self, handler: impl FnMut(&AppEvent, &mut dyn EventActions) + 'static) -> EventRouter`: What the app does when events were dropped: re-read the state it mirrors.
- `pub fn register_all(&self, port: &mut dyn EventsPort) -> Vec<String>`: Register every interest; the refusals come back as sentences (the app shows them).
- `pub fn begin(&mut self, port: &mut dyn EventsPort, acts: &mut dyn EventActions) -> usize`: Start the app's event stream: what waited is handled now, before the first frame.
- `pub fn pump(&mut self, port: &mut dyn EventsPort, acts: &mut dyn EventActions) -> usize`: Handle what arrived. Returns how many events were handled.
- `pub fn recover(&mut self, port: &mut dyn EventsPort, acts: &mut dyn EventActions) -> usize`: After a crash: handle what was delivered but not handled (the numbers after the last one this router saw).
- `pub fn last_seq(&self) -> u64`
- `pub fn resume_after(&mut self, seq: u64)`: The app handed in the last number it had saved (after a restart).

### struct `MemEvents`

An in-memory port with the core's rules. The test says which events the app holds the scope for, moves the clock and makes events
happen with [`MemEvents::happen`].

```rust
pub struct MemEvents
```

Public fields:

- `pub published: Vec<(String, EvPayload)>`

Methods:

- `pub fn new() -> MemEvents`
- `pub fn allow(&mut self, event: &str)`: The app holds the scope for this event.
- `pub fn allow_publish(&mut self)`
- `pub fn coalescing(&mut self, event: &str)`: Only the latest of this event waits.
- `pub fn rate_limit(&mut self, event: &str, per_min: u32)`
- `pub fn set_time(&mut self, ms: u64)`
- `pub fn hold(&mut self, names: &[&str])`: The app holds these names now (what `capabilities` answers).
- `pub fn permission_change(&mut self, granted: &[&str], revoked: &[&str], by: &str, restart: bool)`: What the core does when something changes what the app may do: the event is queued (no registration is needed), later changes are added up, and an event the app is no longer allowed to hear is dropped with its registration.
- `pub fn pending(&self) -> usize`
- `pub fn happen(&mut self, event: &str, payload: EvPayload)`: Something happened: queued if the app registered, holds the scope and the person has not switched it off.
- `pub fn switch(&mut self, event: &str, on: bool)`: The person's switch in Settings.
